subject: AWS Marketplace AMI licensing, localization assets, and procurement checklist
messages:
From: Amy Sutherland <amy.sutherland@bechtel.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@bechtel.com
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Quick Qs on AWS listing AMI licensing + localization

Hi Priyom / Kimberly,

Thanks for the initial walkthrough today. A couple of quick items procurement asked me to confirm before we move to approval:

- AMI licensing: does your AMI require any additional license keys post-subscription, or is everything covered by the marketplace purchase? We need clear language for our procurement terms.
- Regional AMIs: we operate in multiple AWS regions; do you publish separate AMIs per region (us-west-2, us-east-1) or provide a global AMI alias?
- Localization: our field teams will want a short Spanish one-liner for the product tile. Can you share the 1-line and a 2-sentence description that we can use in our internal purchase justification?

If easier, we can route the AMI/ops questions to your marketplace contact. We need answers by COB Tuesday to stay on our procurement cadence.

Thanks,
Amy
Amy Sutherland
IT Sourcing Manager | Bechtel
amy.sutherland@bechtel.com

--

From: priyom_das@redwood.com <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Amy Sutherland <amy.sutherland@bechtel.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 08:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick Qs on AWS listing AMI licensing + localization

Hi Amy — thanks for the clear list. Answers inline below and attaching the marketplace checklist and AMI manifest for your procurement/legal team.

1) AMI licensing: The marketplace purchase is the licensing mechanism. There are no additional license keys or activation steps after a successful AWS Marketplace subscription. We surface the license terms on the product page and include a brief EULA PDF inside the AMI. For procurement language you can use: "License granted by subscription via AWS Marketplace; no further activation required."

2) Regional AMIs: We publish region-specific AMIs. The AMI manifest (attached) lists the current region mappings for us-east-1, us-west-2 and eu-west-1. We also provide automated replication for additional regions on request; that replication SLA is in the marketplace private offer if you want guaranteed availability in a new region.

3) Localization: Suggested text below — short one-liner (Spanish) + two-sentence description (English):
- One-line (ES): "Plataforma de inferencia de alto rendimiento para desplegar modelos de lenguaje a escala."
- Two-sentence (EN): "Redwood Inference ofrece una runtime optimizada para inferencia de LLMs con controles de latencia y costo para producción. Soporta despliegues hospedados, capacidad dedicada y opciones privadas (VPC / on‑prem)."

Action items:
- Attached: marketplace_asset_checklist_v3.xlsx (assets + field pack we promised)
- Attached: ami_manifest_v1.json (region -> AMI id mapping)
- Attached: security_evidence_summary.pdf (SOC & audit notes)

Kimberly — can you confirm the final product tile headline we plan to publish? Naomi / Aditya — FYI on procurement ask and localization snippet.

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0192

Cc: Amy Sutherland <amy.sutherland@bechtel.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick Qs on AWS listing AMI licensing + localization

Thanks — good, clear answers Priyom. A couple of follow-ups from the marketplace/ops perspective:

- Product tile headline: proposing "Redwood Inference — Production LLM Inference Platform" (short) and a slightly shorter elevator: "High-performance LLM inference with predictable latency and cost." If Bechtel prefers more field-focused language we can swap to "Enterprise LLM inference for regulated workloads."
- Legal footnote: procurement will likely ask for the data retention and logs language. I added a short boilerplate we publish on the listing: "Redwood Inference retains request-level telemetry for up to 30 days; audit logs available to enterprise customers under Private deployment agreements." Can you confirm that is acceptable for procurement?
- AMI visibility: Naomi, please double-check the ami_manifest for the us-east-1 AMI ID and confirm the snapshot visibility settings are set to public for marketplace ingestion. If not, we need a quick ops task to correct before onboarding.

Amy — tagging you so procurement sees the suggested tile and footnote; we can swap any language you need for your internal approval docs.

Kimberly Park
Marketplace Partnerships Lead | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Forwarding the ingestion checklist and the final onboarding link. Please ensure the following before we schedule the ingestion window:

1) AMI public visibility confirmed for marketplace ingestion (or provide a cross-account snapshot role).
2) Marketplace asset manifest uploaded to the portal (we validated the file names but will need the public S3 link).
3) One-line and extended descriptions provided (we saw the ES one-liner; please submit the final English copy in the portal).
4) Proof of license (EULA PDF is fine) and security evidence (SOC/ISO summaries).

Link to intake: https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/ingest/launch/ENVELOPE-999999

Please reply-all with a quick checklist status — if everything is green we can book ingestion for Nov 23rd.

Thanks,
Marketplace Onboarding Team
AWS Marketplace
